text:
maria: Quick design ping — I'm prototyping an "otel bootstrapper" pattern for our inference services. Idea: a tiny, language-agnostic init layer (shared binary or tiny sidecar) that standardizes OTEL SDK bootstrap, resource detection, and graceful flush so Python/Go/Rust runners behave the same. Motivation: too many ad-hoc init differences, dead exporters on SIGTERM, and inconsistent span attrs across runtimes.

raj: curious — how would it work for private deployments where we can't run extra containers? sidecar might be hard.

maria: good call. plan is dual-mode: 1) in-process shim (lib with identical semantic defaults per lang) 2) optional sidecar/agent mode we can enable for hosted/dedicated. the key is a deterministic bootstrap policy file (yaml) that each runtime reads on startup.

alice: policy file = interesting. must include exporter fanout config, per-tenant routing, and buffering windows. we need sane defaults for batch_size, export_timeout, and max_queue. also we should expose a "flush_on_shutdown: true" flag.

kevin: sampling and kv-cache spans: we need a consistent sampling decision surface so a request sampled in Python is sampled the same when it hits a Rust microservice. how do we propagate that? currently we have half the libs using traceflags and others using our custom header.

maria: agreed. plan: standardize on W3C traceparent + a small extra header `x-rw-sample` for deterministic backend sampling (boolean + sampler-version). bootstrapper will set that if local sampler says yes.

elaine: UX ask: product needs a quick toggle to reduce retention per-team during incidents. can policy include retention overrides tied to tenant-id and a rollout flag? need it accessible from the Console.

maria: yes — policy supports match rules (tenant_id, env, service_name) and actions: {sampler_rate, retention_days, exporter_endpoint_override}. Console will edit/broadcast policy via S3/kms or CP, bootstrapper polls or watches.

raj: runtime concerns: languages differ for global SDK lifecycle. Python and Go have different shutdown windows (goroutines vs interpreter exit). any cross-lang shim must handle graceful drain on SIGTERM and on process manager kills.

maria: prototype shim does: register SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers, start a 30s draining window, call SDK.force_flush(timeout=10s), then exit. for languages that don't allow handlers (some FFI edgecases) the sidecar mode becomes the fallback.

kevin: can we show the python snippet for the in-process shim?

maria: sure:
```python
# bootstrapper init (python)
from rw_otel_bootstrap import init_bootstrapper
init_bootstrapper(policy_path='/etc/rw/otel-policy.yaml', service_name='inference-runtime')
# init_bootstrapper handles resource detection, sampler, env-based exporter, and SIGTERM flush
```

raj: go example?

maria:
```go
// main.go
func main(){
  cfg := rwotel.LoadPolicy("/etc/rw/otel-policy.yaml")
  sh := rwotel.Bootstrap(cfg) // returns Shutdown func() error
  defer sh() // ensures flush on normal exit
  // run server...
}
```

kevin: rust?

maria: Rust will expose a tiny crate with an async shutdown hook:
```rust
let guard = rw_otel_bootstrap::bootstrap("/etc/rw/otel-policy.yaml").await?;
// guard.flush_and_shutdown().await on ctrlc
```

alice: one more tough part — exporter credentials and multitenant fanout. we must avoid leaking tenant secrets. policy should support binding exporter credentials to service identity (VM role / KMS wrapped creds) rather than embedding them in the config. sidecar mode can hold KMS keys and perform per-tenant fanout safely.

elaine: does this affect trace attribute size? Console dashboards rely on route and model attributes. we should cap attribute name lengths and have a whitelist in policy to avoid exploding span sizes.

maria: will default to whitelist + attribute-size cap (256 chars). also provide a transform hook so services can apply deterministic redaction.

raj: opentelemetry SDK specifics: some languages buffer spans in thread-local queues then flush. we've seen memory spikes when batch_size is large. policy should allow "max_inflight_spans" per-process.

maria: adding that. also proposing a health-check endpoint for the bootstrapper so infra can detect when exporters are blocked/backed up. health: {queue_depth, last_export_status}.

kevin: observability: we need meta-spans for "kvcache.lookup" and "kvspan" naming consistency. propose names: rw.kv.lookup and rw.kv.hit (bool). please standardize in the shim so tracing queries show up uniformly.

elaine: rollout plan? start with a non-invasive mode: shim emits but does not change sampling. then ramp to enforced policy + sidecar in hosted. we should provide an easy opt-out flag per service for until stable.

maria: exactly — canary steps: dev env -> infra services -> batch rollout to customer-facing inference clusters. will add telemetry checks to ensure no regression.

raj: one more: testing the shutdown flush under high qps is tricky. recommend a harness to synthesize 100k traces/sec and ensure exporter drains within policy timeout. we should add that to perf CI.

maria: added to backlog. @alice can you own sidecar credential design? @raj can you validate Go shutdown semantics in the prototype? @kevin can you draft the kvspan naming doc?

alice: yep, will take sidecar creds.

raj: I'll validate Go and Linux signal interplay.

kevin: will draft kv span naming and sampling headers.

elaine: I'll design the Console toggle UX and retention override APIs.

otel-bot: deploybot: note: telemetry policy v0.1 pushed to s3://redwood-internal/otel-policy-schema/v0.1 at 1745001200

maria: thanks all. leaving the thread here; will post a short RFC with the policy schema and a PoC link in ~48h. :thumbsup:
